packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-17 - blind first reading (unverified image reading)

Exposure statement: no proposed identification or reading of this record was in my context before reading. The brief and PROMPT.md only. I did nothing beyond the rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- Two separate paper pieces photographed on black, with ruler at top and colour checker bottom right.
- Upper piece: landscape, heavily stained, holed, fold creases (vertical centre, horizontal lower). No main-text writing visible on this face at overview scale. Modern pencil notes: at left, written vertically, "Stams, STA, Fig. 174-1r" (shelfmark-style label); in centre, written vertically in pencil, a note reading roughly "ad ... [?] Cod. XIII n. 1 / ... 117 / (Chronik ...)" - modern archival annotation, not main text.
- Lower piece: landscape, similarly damaged. Left half blank apart from modern pencil note (horizontal): roughly "Umschlag? / ... Cod XIII n. 1 / (117 ...) / (Chronik ...) ... 16" and at bottom "Stams, STA, Fig. 174-2r" (pencil label). Right half (right of a vertical fold) carries writing in brown ink in an early-modern cursive hand, single block, approx. 25 lines, written across the right panel. Partway down is a tabular list: names in a left sub-column with numbers in a right sub-column (e.g. "Ceci ... 173", "Claudi", "Contracti", "Muti", "Surdi", "Paralytici", "Manus aridae"), then a larger line beginning with an enlarged "M" ("Multa et alia signa ..."). To the right of the list further cursive lines run down the right edge, partly over damage.
- Tentative interpretation: a working/draft note (perhaps a tally of miracles by category) jotted on a reused sheet or wrapper; the two pieces look like halves of a folded wrapper. Not a formal book hand; no rubrics, no ruling visible.
- Only the overview image may be available; detail reading below depends on further tiles.

TILE image-002.jpg (top-left of upper piece, native resolution)
- No ink text. Pencil label written vertically: "Stams, STA, Frag. 174-1r" (correcting "Fig." in survey to "Frag."). Paper with holes, stains, folded top edge.

TILE image-003.jpg (top-centre of upper piece)
- No ink text. Holes and stains. At lower right, start of the vertical modern pencil note: "...X[III] .n. 1" / "...117" (cut off by tile edge).

TILE image-004.jpg (top-right of upper piece)
- Blank: no ink or pencil text. Stains, one hole, tear at upper left (overlaps tile 003).

TILE image-005.jpg (top-right corner of upper piece)
- Blank: no ink or pencil text.

TILE image-006.jpg (middle-left of upper piece; overlaps 002 at top, "Sta[ms]" label visible)
- Blank apart from the overlapping pencil label. Horizontal fold line near bottom. No ink.

TILE image-007.jpg (centre of upper piece)
- No ink. Modern German pencil note, written vertically (read with image rotated, bottom-to-top), three lines:
  007 pencil l.1: als Einband zum Cod(ex) XIII .n. [1? cut at tile top; overview shows "1"]
  007 pencil l.2: oder [?]s 117   (word after "oder" uncertain - "des"? ; possibly "oder Cod. 117"? leave uncertain)
  007 pencil l.3: (Chronik [?]. G[?]...)   - abbreviated, illegible beyond "Chronik"
  This is an archival note ("as binding for Cod. XIII n. 1 ..."), not text of the fragment. Fold lines visible.

TILE image-008.jpg (centre-right of upper piece; overlaps 007 at left - "(Chronik ...)" pencil repeated)
- No ink text. Stains, holes. Overlap only.

TILE image-009.jpg (middle-right edge of upper piece)
- Blank: no ink or pencil.

TILE image-010.jpg (lower-left of upper piece with its repair tape; top-left of lower piece)
- Blank: no ink or pencil text on either piece in this tile. Upper piece bottom edge repaired with transparent tape. Lower piece top-left corner holed.
- Note: the tiles appear to be a grid over the whole photograph spanning both pieces.

TILE image-011.jpg (gap between pieces, centre; top of lower piece left of the vertical fold)
- No text except, at right edge below the vertical fold, the beginnings of the ink lines of the written panel: initial letters only, "A[?]" / "C[?]" / "D[?]" stacked (line-initials of the right-panel text; read in later tiles).

TILE image-012.jpg (top of the written right panel of the lower piece, left half of the text block)
Hand: brown-ink early-modern cursive (humanistic/Kurrent-influenced Latin cursive), quick and irregular, with big looped flourishes from the right side crossing lines. Line-initial letters in the left margin (a column of capitals/marks: "5"?, "A", "D"?, "Dis."). Lines numbered from the top of this tile's text (tile top is upper piece/gap).
 012 l.1 (torn top edge, fragmentary): [flourish] ... L[?]g[?] ... [illegible, cut by tear]
 012 l.2: Dec(?) ff[?] dr(?) ſoſpes(?) bi[?](?) ... [illegible]   - very uncertain, letters damaged along tear
 012 l.3: [margin z/3?] a ūſdrūcket(?) coie(?) vo(?) dom, appe[...]   - reading uncertain; "coie" may be co(mmun)i(t)e(r) with mark; "dom," with comma
 012 l.4: [margin "5"? and a large looped initial] A[d]dere, calcar curenti non [...]   ("curenti" spelled with single r as written)
 012 l.5: [margin "A"] amata(?) flo[ß?]er(?) suffragane(?)[...]   - "suffragane" uncertain: letters look "suppacanc" with ff/pp ambiguity
 012 interlinear above l.6 (small, between l.5 and l.6): [?]n[?]lbn[?]stq(?) - illegible small addition
 012 l.6: [margin flourish "S"/"I"?] [?]debitantibq(ue)(?) ü(?) regione umbra m[ortis? - cut at tile edge]
 012 l.7: [margin "Dis."?] Regio mortis, carcer opacus.
 012 l.8: [?]ūntiū(?) g[?]dium(?) [underlined?]   Nativitas [...]
 012 l.9 (bottom edge, cut): [illegible]
- A large flourish (descender from line 4 to 6 area at right) crosses the text; probably a pen-flourish of a capital in the right half.

TILE image-013.jpg (top-right of written panel; overlaps 012 at left - line ends of 012 continue here). Lines aligned to 012 numbering:
 013 l.1 (torn top, faint): [illegible] ... A[?] ... ſe[?] ... [illegible]   - abraded and torn
 013 l.2: [?]e(?) [?]b[?]es(?) [?]exspt[?](?) [?]ſ[?] [illegible] [?]n[?]   - faint, abraded
 013 l.3: (...dom,) appſ[?]ſ[?](?) [?]e(?) de gaudente(?)s(?) [?] [?]e[?]   - uncertain; continues 012 l.3 "appe..."
 013 l.4: (...curenti) non [large S-flourish over a word: "op?"]us est. ſic incitare ad[...]
 013 l.5: (...suffragane?)ncq(ue)(?) [S-flourish] ſed(?) id quod reſemq(?) [?]hon[?][...]   - "reſemq" may be a contracted word; unresolved
 013 l.6: (...)umbra mortis. en locus [large looped flourish] loc[a?][...]
 013 l.7: (...)opacus. civitasq(ue)(?) obſeſſa sine vic[...]   - final letter of "civita-" has a q-like stroke: "civitas" + q(ue)? or "civitas" with long s? uncertain
 013 l.8: (Na)tivitas tua Dej(?) genit[?]e(?) Virg[...]   - "Dej" initial is a looped capital that could also be R; "genit-" ends in an abbreviated form, read as visible
 013 l.9 (cut at bottom): [flourishes] [illegible]
- Right edge has transparent repair tape; line-ends lost/obscured beyond "ad", "[?]hon", "loc", "vic", "Virg".

TILE image-014.jpg (middle-left of lower piece)
- No ink. Start of modern pencil note (horizontal): "entnommen" (?) / "Cod. XIII n[...]" / "(117 H[...]" / "(Chronik [...]" - continued in next tile. Archival note, not fragment text.

TILE image-015.jpg (centre of lower piece, left of vertical fold; overlaps 014)
- No ink text. Modern pencil note completes:
  015 pencil l.1: [entn]ommen(?) d(em) Einband
  015 pencil l.2: Cod. XIII n. 1
  015 pencil l.3: (117 H[s?])
  015 pencil l.4: [(Chro]nik [?] [?]ay[?] -)   } de an[n]i(?) 16   - the bracketed note "de ani 16" (?) beside a brace; uncertain
- At top right edge, line-initial strokes of the written panel (overlap with 016).

TILE image-016.jpg (left half of written panel, middle; top three lines overlap 012 l.6-8 - not new text)
 016 l.1 (=012 l.6): [large looped initial, I/S?]nhabitantibq(?) / [?]debitantibq ū(?) regione umbra m[...]   - clearer here: the letter after the initial is d- or h-shaped; the word may be "-habitantib(us)q(ue)" with q-mark; "ū/ü" is a single short word, possibly ī(n). Leaving both readings visible.
 016 l.1 interlinear above (=012 interlinear): [?]n[?]lbn[?]st[?] - still illegible
 016 l.2 (=012 l.7): [margin "Dis." or "Iis."] Regio mortis, carcer opacus,
 016 l.3 (=012 l.8): [?]ūntid(?) [ga]udium(?)  - the first syllable "ga" looks struck through by a horizontal stroke; a long flourish under "-um" sweeps to the right    Nativitas [...]
 016 l.3a (lower-left, small, beneath l.3 start): u[?]m[?]a(?) - faint word beginning, possibly part of l.3 continuing at margin
 016 l.4: [large flourished capital A/R]bba[?]l[?]s(?) [?]iij(?)     [?]and(?) Johannes(?)   - "Johannes" written with a looped J, then a small mark "z" below
 016 l.5 (indented): S. Bern. in peregrinatio[n]e(?) (written "peregrinatoe" with suspension) ge[...]
 --- tabular list (indented, one word per line; numbers in right sub-column fall in tile 017):
 016 l.6:  Ceci .sanati(?)   - "Ceci" = Caeci; second word could be "sanati" or "sancti"; I see s-a-n-a/c-t-i, a dot before it
 016 l.7:  Claudi.
 016 l.8:  Contracti
 016 l.9:  Muti
 016 l.10: Surdj.
 016 l.11: Paralytici .
 016 l.12: Manus aridæ (written "aridæ"/"aridae" with e-ligature)
 016 l.13 (further indented, smaller): Aliaq(ue)(?) [i]nnumerabilia(?)   - first letters "Aliaſ d" then "numerabilia"; "innumerabilia" plausible but the "in-" is not clearly written
 016 l.14 (large initial M with flourish): Multa et alia signa f[...]
 016 l.15 (smaller, indented): S. Bergrūſe(?) Prag(?).   - uncertain, flourished; possibly a name/abbreviation
 016 l.16 (bottom edge, cut): [?] [?]antu[?]cri[?]f(?) abstinent[...]

TILE image-017.jpg (right half of written panel, middle; top lines overlap 013 l.6-8)
 017 l.1 (=013 l.6): (...)umbra mortis. en locus [flourish] loc[...]
 017 l.2 (=013 l.7): (...)opacus. civitasq(ue)(?) obſeſſa sine vic[...]
 017 l.3 (=013 l.8): (Na)tivitas tua Dej(?) genit[ri]x(?) Virg[...]   - "genit-" ends with a nasal/abbrev. stroke; then "Virg" partly behind a hole, followed by flourishes
 017 l.4 (continues 016 l.4 "...Johannes"): (Jo)hannes dahe(?) auf(?) an(?) [?]m(?) [?]ſ[?]   - looks like German words in the same cursive ("daher auf ein"?), very uncertain; trailing flourishes
 017 l.5 (continues 016 l.5): (pere)grinatoē(?) germania fecit miracula
 --- numbers column of the list (aligned to 016 l.6-12):
 017 l.6:  173.      (Ceci sanati)
